findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds a new gitlink (mode 160000) at path 'sentry-repo' pointing to commit a5d290951de with no corresponding .gitmodules entry anywhere in the repository. The submodule reference is unresolvable: `git submodule init/update` fails with 'no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules', and any CI checkout configured with submodules cannot fetch commit a5d290951de from a named remote, breaking the build before any code runs. This is an accidental artifact (e.g. a stray nested clone) committed alongside an unrelated pyproject change and must be removed.

[BUG] The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction aggregates `Column("sample_weight")`, but the diff adds no Snuba entity schema, migration, or writer that defines or populates a `sample_weight` column. Every query transformed by `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` (i.e. every events-stats request from an allowlisted project) sends a SnQL aggregate over a column that does not exist in the events schema; Snuba rejects it with an invalid-column error, turning the 200 stats response into a 400/500 for exactly the projects the feature targets. The comment 'assumes sample_weight exists ... as per schema design' asserts a prerequisite that nothing in this PR (or the diff's own test factory) establishes.

[BUG] The factory helper writes `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` from `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate`, while the query transform reads a column named `sample_weight` — the names never meet, and `sample_rate` as a top-level event field is not a recognized field that maps to any Snuba column. Even granting the schema exists, the test data path can never populate the column `sum(sample_weight)` aggregates, so the new API tests' core assertion (`data[0][1][0]["count"] == 10`, i.e. 1 event / 0.1 rate) depends on a value nothing writes; the tests can only pass by accident of the mocked options or fail outright, and the shared `store_event` mutation silently injects a non-schema field into every test event in the codebase.

[BUG] `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` references an option key that is not registered in sentry/options/defaults.py anywhere in this diff. `options.get` raises `UnknownOption` for unregistered keys, so the first organization-events-stats request after deploy crashes with a 500 until an options registration lands; the new tests all mock `options` and therefore cannot detect this.

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` does a raw substring check (`"event.type:error" in query`), which is True for negated filters like `!event.type:error` that select transactions only. A user querying the discover dataset with `!event.type:error` on allowlisted projects gets `count()` rewritten to `upsampled_count()` over transaction events, where sample_weight does not exist — the request fails at Snuba or returns upsampled counts for non-error data. The new test only covers `event.type:transaction`, not the negated-error form, so the bug ships untested.

[ADVISORY] The 'performance optimization' adds a cache.get and cache.set (remote Redis/memcached round-trips via sentry.utils.cache) to every organization-events-stats request in order to memoize `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, whose only work is an in-memory `options.get` dict lookup. The highest-traffic stats endpoint in the product gains two remote cache I/O operations per request to avoid a local dict read — a net hot-path regression, directly contradicting the PR's performance claim; operators get added Redis load and latency on every dashboard refresh.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` ships with no caller anywhere in the diff — no allowlist-change path, management command, or UI ever invokes it. Ships-inert: the documented invalidation contract ('should be called when the allowlist configuration changes') cannot be honored; the only real invalidation is the 60-second TTL, so allowlist revocations silently keep serving upsampled (inflated) counts for up to a minute and the dead function misleads maintainers into assuming eager invalidation exists.

[ADVISORY] The identical two-line block `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` is hand-repeated at three separate execution branches (RPC top-events, RPC plain, standard), even though `upsampling_enabled` and `query_columns` are already fixed at the top of the function. The next person adding a fourth execution branch (or changing the transformation) must remember to replicate the block in each arm or silently serve un-upsampled counts on that path; transforming once right after `upsampling_enabled` is computed deletes three conditional blocks and all three places-to-update.

[ADVISORY] `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` accepts an `organization` parameter it never reads, and its docstring's NOTE about 'configuration changing during request processing' describes behavior the code does not have (the option is read exactly once per call). Callers and reviewers reasonably infer organization-scoped allowlist validation is happening; a future change that needs org scoping will assume the parameter is already wired up, and the stale NOTE sends maintainers hunting for mid-request re-reads that don't exist.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` itself — the only exported entry point and the only code containing stateful cache behavior (the `cached_result is not None` short-circuit branch and the cache.set path) — while the tests cover only the private helpers. A regression in the cache logic (e.g. a non-boolean cached value, or the `cached_result and _should_apply...` short-circuit wrongly skipping the dataset check) would pass the entire new test suite, since `test_error_upsampling.py` imports `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` but never the cached wrapper the endpoint actually calls.

[ADVISORY] The `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered without `private=True`, making it a user-callable aggregation on every discover-dataset query, while it hard-depends on a `sample_weight` column that only exists (at best) for allowlisted error projects. Any customer can now send `yAxis=upsampled_count()` (e.g. via saved dashboards or the stats API) for any project; queries on non-allowlisted projects or transaction data hit the missing column and return a Snuba error to the user, generating unexplained 4xx/5xx support load. Marking the function `private` (as the neighboring `count_if`-style internal functions in the same converter do) would remove it from the public surface.

[BUG] The `upsampled_count` SnQL function is registered only in the discover dataset, but `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset (error_upsampling.py lines 113-114: `if dataset == errors: return True`), so errors-dataset queries receive `upsampled_count() as count` while errors.py's function_converter has no such function. Any events-stats query routed to the errors dataset for an allowlisted organization fails with an unknown-function error from the SnQL parser instead of returning upsampled counts; the helper's own code path explicitly enables this branch, so it is a live path in the artifact's design, not a hypothetical.

[BUG] `_is_error_focused_query` decides error-focus by raw substring match (`if "event.type:error" in query`), which matches negated queries like `!event.type:error` and quoted text like `message:"event.type:error"`. For an allowlisted org, a query like `!event.type:error` (or a message search containing that literal) gets `count()` rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over a discover result set that includes transaction rows where the sample_weight column does not exist, so the request fails in snuba or returns silently wrong counts; there is no test in the diff covering negated or quoted queries.

[ADVISORY] For the discover dataset, upsampling is applied only when the query string contains the literal `event.type:error`, so discover queries that include errors without that token (empty query, `error.handled:false`, `user.email:x`) silently skip the transformation. The same allowlisted org's errors are counted raw in default/unfiltered charts and weighted in error-filtered charts, producing inconsistent numbers between adjacent dashboard widgets on identical data; the limitation lives only in a helper docstring and is not surfaced to operators or covered by a test asserting the unweighted fallback for an unfiltered query.

[ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is dead code: no caller for it exists anywhere in the diff, so the docstring's contract ("should be called when the allowlist configuration changes") is never honored. After an operator changes the allowlist, every served events-stats request for affected orgs keeps returning the stale eligibility decision for up to 60 seconds (and the single-key design cannot invalidate across processes anyway), yielding wrong counts with a helper that implies consistency; the next reader of the code is misled into thinking invalidation is wired up.

[ADVISORY] The top_events branch of `_get_event_stats` with upsampling enabled (both the `use_rpc` `run_top_events_timeseries_query` path and the non-RPC `top_events_timeseries` path, where the transformed columns feed `timeseries_columns` alongside untransformed `selected_columns`, `raw_groupby`, and `orderby`) is never exercised by any test in the diff. All four new endpoint tests omit the `topEvents` parameter, so a regression in the highest-traffic branch — e.g., the hardcoded `as count` alias colliding with top-events ordering, or `upsampled_count` being rejected by the top-events query builder — would ship undetected and break the org-level top-events graph for allowlisted orgs.

[ADVISORY] No test covers `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` itself — the imports at lines 14-19 show only the private helpers are tested — leaving the 60-second cache logic (cache-hit early return at error_upsampling.py lines 30-31, the `cache.set` write, and the interaction of a warm cache with changed options) entirely unverified. A defect in the cache path — e.g., the eligibility decision being served stale after an allowlist change, or the hit-path boolean short-circuit behaving differently from the miss-path — would ship with a green suite; the API tests only pass because each creates a fresh org and therefore always misses the cache, never exercising the cached branch that production traffic will overwhelmingly hit.

[BUG] The option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` is read via `options.get` but is never registered anywhere in this diff (no addition to sentry's options registry), so unless it pre-exists outside the diff, `options.get` always returns the default `[]` in production. The feature is silently inert in production — `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` returns False for every request — while all four API tests mock `options` wholesale and therefore never verify that the real option resolves; operators setting the allowlist would see no behavioral change and no error.

[BUG] The diff adds a git submodule named `sentry-repo` pinned to a5d290951de, with no code, test, or documentation in the diff referencing it. CI checkouts and developer clones that do not initialize submodules break or silently skip this path, and the feature (error upsampling) has no dependency that requires vendoring a repository snapshot — this is an accidental commit that should be removed from the PR.

[ADVISORY] The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered without `private=True`, unlike its neighboring aggregation functions in the same converter, so it becomes directly selectable by any user query on the discover dataset. Any organization (allowlisted or not) can pass `yAxis=upsampled_count()` to discover endpoints and receive raw `sum(sample_weight)` values that are meaningless for non-allowlisted projects (whose events carry no meaningful weight), producing confusing numbers and expanding the public query surface with no gating; it also hardcodes the alias `count`, overriding whatever alias a direct caller supplies.

[BUG] The PR commits a new git submodule pointer ('sentry-repo' at a5d290951de) at the repository root, which is unrelated to the upsampling feature. An accidental nested-checkout artifact is added to the repo: CI/clone behavior changes for every developer and pipeline, and the diff carries a piece of state no requirement asks for. This is untraceable scope drift and should be removed from the PR.

[BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for the errors dataset, but the 'upsampled_count' SnQL function it emits is only registered in discover.py's function_converter (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1041-1052), leaving the errors-dataset path referencing an unregistered function. Any request that selects dataset=errors with all projects allowlisted gets its count() rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count', which the errors dataset's resolver cannot parse, so the query fails at SnQL compilation instead of returning stats — a 4xx/5xx on a query that worked before the allowlist was populated.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second eligibility cache is speculative over-engineering with no traceable requirement: it caches a single options.get() call (already served from Sentry's in-memory options store) and its own docstring contradicts _are_all_projects_error_upsampled's claim of reading configuration 'fresh each time'. The codebase gains a cache key format, TTL semantics, and staleness window that no requirement asked for; operators get up to 60s of stale eligibility decisions after an allowlist change, and future readers must reason about a cache consistency model that exists to optimize a lookup that was never measured as slow. Deleting the cache layer (keeping _are_all_projects_error_upsampled) removes the staleness risk and the entire invalidation problem.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code: no caller exists anywhere in this diff, so the docstring's 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes' contract is never honored. Future maintainers reading the docstring will assume invalidation is wired up and rely on cache consistency that does not exist; ships-inert public surface that either needs a caller (wherever the allowlist option is mutated) or deletion.

[ADVISORY] Nothing in this diff produces the sample_weight column that the upsampled_count aggregation sums; the only producer added is a test-factory side effect that writes a different field ('sample_rate') into normalized_data, so the helper's 'schema ensures sample_weight exists' assumption is enforced by nothing. The aggregation's core invariant (every event in an allowlisted project carries a sample_weight) has no ingestion-side implementation and no test exercising the real field; when real allowlisted projects contain events predating the feature (or ingested without the error_sampling context), sum(sample_weight) silently drops them and reported counts deflate. The factory change also mutates shared store_event behavior for every test that sets an error_sampling context, a blast radius beyond this feature's needs.

[ADVISORY] _is_error_focused_query decides eligibility by substring match of 'event.type:error' anywhere in the lowercased raw query string, so queries that merely contain the token (e.g. 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction', or a message search containing the literal text) are treated as error-only. A mixed error+transaction query over allowlisted projects gets count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight); transaction events have no sample_weight, so the transaction portion of the chart collapses to 0/NULL while the endpoint reports a 200 — silently wrong numbers rather than an error.

[ADVISORY] The transformation is applied only inside _get_event_stats of this one endpoint via a three-branch duplicated pattern ('if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform(...)' repeated at ~226, ~275, ~294) plus a redundant 'upsampling_enabled = should_upsample' alias, when a single pre-branch transform would suffice. Every future query-execution branch added to this function must remember to repeat the transform or it silently serves unupsampled counts; the deletion test passes cleanly — one transform call before the top_events/use_rpc branching makes all three conditional blocks and the alias unnecessary.

[ADVISORY] Under-scoping: the upsampling transform is wired into only this endpoint's stats path, while the same org/project/time-range counts served by other surfaces (events tables, dashboard widgets backed by other endpoints) still use raw count(). For an allowlisted project, the graph shows the upsampled count (e.g. 10) while the adjacent issue list or event table for the same window shows the raw count (e.g. 1) — internally inconsistent numbers presented to users as if one were wrong; the helper is written as a general facility but is reachable from exactly one call site in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The PR changes an unrelated user-facing error message ('If topEvents needs to be at least 1' -> 'topEvents needs to be at least 1') with no traceable requirement. Unrelated drive-by change: any test, snapshot, or client string-matching on the old message breaks without this feature needing the change; it should be a separate PR or dropped.

[ADVISORY] The new cache state machine (cache-hit branch returning 'cached_result and _should_apply...', the 60s TTL set, and invalidate_upsampling_cache) has zero test coverage: all tests either call the private helpers directly or mock options entirely, so the caching logic added for 'performance' is never executed against a real or stubbed cache. A regression in the cache-hit branch (e.g. returning the cached bool without re-checking dataset, or caching after the dataset check) would ship undetected; the only untested code in the new module is precisely the layer the PR headline advertises as its performance optimization.

[BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, but the upsampled_count SnQLFunction is only registered in the discover dataset's function_converter, so allowlisted errors-dataset queries are transformed to a function the errors dataset cannot resolve. Every request to the events-stats endpoint with dataset=errors from an allowlisted project gets its yAxis rewritten to 'upsampled_count() as count', which ErrorsDataset has no SnQLFunction for; the query build fails and the user gets an error (or the function silently resolves to nothing) on all error-dataset charts for allowlisted orgs. This is a parallel-path contradiction: the eligibility gate and the function registry disagree about which datasets support the feature.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses a raw substring check ('event.type:error' in query), which matches negated and OR-composed conditions like '!event.type:error' or 'event.type:transaction OR event.type:error', classifying non-error queries as error-focused. A discover-dataset query excluding errors (e.g. '!event.type:error', which returns transaction events) gets count() rewritten to sum(sample_weight) over transaction rows where the sample_weight semantics do not exist, producing wrong counts or a query failure for exactly the queries the guard was written to exclude.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling emits sum(sample_weight) with no coalesce/default and no check that sample_weight is populated, relying on an assertion ('database schema to ensure sample_weight exists for all events') that nothing in the diff enforces or backfills. Events ingested before the sampling rollout, or by SDKs that never send contexts.error_sampling (note: the test factory only sets sample_rate when that context is present), carry NULL/zero sample_weight; for such rows sum(sample_weight) yields NULL/0, so an allowlisted project's error counts silently collapse toward 0 on the stats chart instead of reflecting stored events. The factory hook's conditional ('if client_sample_rate:') is itself evidence the field is not universally present.

[BUG] In the top-events path only timeseries_columns/y_axes are transformed; selected_columns (self.get_field_list), equations (self.get_equation_list), and orderby (self.get_orderby) are passed through untransformed, so any of them referencing count() computes the raw sampled count while the displayed series uses the upsampled count. A topEvents request ordered by count() ranks groups by the raw sampled count while displaying the upsampled count, and equation-based y-axes mix raw and upsampled aggregates in one formula — the chart shows numbers whose ranking and arithmetic are internally inconsistent for allowlisted orgs.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second cache is a speculative optimization that adds a memcache network roundtrip to every events-stats request to avoid an in-memory options.get dict lookup, and its companion invalidate_upsampling_cache (lines 67-76) has no caller anywhere in the diff and structurally cannot work. Every request pays a cache roundtrip plus key-construction cost to save a nanosecond-scale local lookup; the invalidation function is dead code, and even if wired up, its key embeds hash(sorted(project_ids)) of one specific combination, so it cannot invalidate the unbounded set of other project-subset keys an org queries with — the 'cache consistency' promised in its docstring is unachievable by design. Deleting the cache layer removes the roundtrip, the dead function, and the staleness window entirely.

[ADVISORY] The _are_all_projects_error_upsampled docstring states it 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time' and 'can return different results between calls', but its only caller caches the result for 60 seconds, so the documented behavior is not the implemented behavior. The next maintainer trusting the docstring (e.g. when reasoning about allowlist-change consistency or wiring the invalidation hook) will design against a freshness guarantee the code does not provide; the docstring and the caching caller make contradictory claims about the same call.

[ADVISORY] The upsampling decision is made by string-munging query columns inside one endpoint instead of at the dataset/search-resolver layer where dataset and project context already live, leaving every other error-count surface for the same org on the raw sampled path. For an allowlisted org, the events-stats chart shows upsampled counts while dashboards built on the organization_events endpoint, issue/search counts, and alert queries over the same time window show raw sampled counts — mutually inconsistent numbers for the same data. Anchoring the transform at the resolver layer (where the discover/errors dataset split and per-project context are already available) would make it apply uniformly and eliminate the endpoint-side dataset-sniffing and substring query parsing altogether.

[ADVISORY] The only code in this diff that writes sample_rate is a test-factory hook reading contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate; no production ingestion/processing path that populates sample_rate (and thus sample_weight) appears in the diff, so the endpoint E2E tests exercise a data path that exists only in tests. The four new endpoint tests go green via a stand-in writer that production requests never traverse; if the real ingestion path does not perform the same contexts.error_sampling -> sample_rate mapping, the feature ships reading a column nothing populates and every allowlisted org's upsampled counts are wrong on day one while CI stays green.

[ADVISORY] The identical 'if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)' block is repeated three times, and should_upsample/upsampling_enabled are two names for the same value computed once. The transformation point can be hoisted to the top next to the eligibility check, deleting two branches and one redundant variable; as written, a future change to the transform invocation (e.g. also transforming orderby) must be replicated in three places and a missed copy silently reintroduces the raw/upssampled inconsistency.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a new git submodule named 'sentry-repo' pinned to commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a at the repository root. A nested checkout of (apparently) the sentry repository inside the sentry repository looks like an accidental commit from a development environment; if merged, it pins an external snapshot into the repo tree, breaks standard checkouts/CI that do not expect it, and creates a confusing second copy of the codebase alongside the real one.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a git submodule 'sentry-repo' pinned to commit a5d290951de, which is not part of the stated feature intent (error-count upsampling). Every contributor cloning the repo gets an unexpected nested checkout of the Sentry source tree pinned to an arbitrary commit; this is an accidental commit of a developer's working directory and silently changes the repository structure without being part of the accepted objective.

[ADVISORY] The PR silently rewrites the user-facing validation error message from "If topEvents needs to be at least 1" to "topEvents needs to be at least 1", an unrelated change smuggled into the upsampling feature. Any client, test, or documentation asserting on the exact 400 detail string breaks without a dedicated decision; this is scope creep inside a performance/feature PR that a reviewer approving 'upsampling support' never explicitly accepted.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses raw substring matching, so negated or compound discover queries such as '!event.type:error' or '(event.type:error OR event.type:transaction)' are classified as error-focused and get count() replaced with sum(sample_weight) over rows that have no sample_weight. For allowlisted projects, a query excluding errors (e.g. !event.type:error on discover) has its transaction counts silently transformed to sum over a missing/zero sample_weight column, returning 0 or a query error instead of the raw counts the non-allowlisted path returns for the identical query.

[BUG] The new upsampled_count SnQLFunction is registered without private=True, converting an internal upsampling mechanism into a user-callable aggregation in the public discover query language. Any user can invoke upsampled_count() in an arbitrary discover query (including event.type:transaction queries on projects that were never allowlisted), where sample_weight does not exist per the function's own stated precondition, producing query errors or misleading numbers that the internal-only design never intended to expose.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the exact literal 'count()' (case/space-normalized), leaving count-derived aggregates such as epm() and failure_rate() in the same yAxis list unsampled. A single response for allowlisted projects returns mutually inconsistent numbers: the count() series is multiplied by the sample weight while the epm()/rate series on the same chart is computed from the raw count, so charts built from one request contradict each other by the sampling factor.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no caller anywhere in the diff, and its org+project-scoped cache key cannot be enumerated for a global sentry option change, so the documented invalidation contract is unfulfillable. An operator flipping 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' gets no invalidation (the docstring promises 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes' but no writer exists); the only real invalidation is the silent 60-second TTL, and the dead function misleads future maintainers into believing consistency is handled.

[ADVISORY] The 60-second cache contradicts both its own comment ('This cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution' — it actually guarantees inconsistent behavior across requests during the TTL window) and the NOTE in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled claiming the config is 'read fresh each time' (the caller caches it, so the fresh-read claim is false). After an operator allowlists or delists a project, up to 60 seconds of responses use the stale classification, and the two docstrings state opposite guarantees; anyone debugging count discrepancies during a rollout is pointed to the wrong mechanism by the in-code documentation.

[ADVISORY] The identical two-line 'if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)' block is duplicated three times (lines ~230, ~275, ~295), and 'upsampling_enabled = should_upsample' is a pure alias with no added meaning. The next change to the transform (e.g. also rewriting epm()) must be applied in three places inside three different branches; hoisting a single transform before the top_events/use_rpc branching deletes two duplicated blocks and the alias variable, and removes the risk of one branch silently diverging.

[ADVISORY] store_event, the shared test factory used by effectively every ingestion test, is permanently mutated to inject 'sample_rate' into any event carrying contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate, with two bare 'except Exception: pass' blocks suppressing all failures. Every existing test in the suite that stores an event with an error_sampling context now silently ingests a different event payload (sample_rate set), changing shared fixture semantics from inside an unrelated feature PR; if the derived sample_rate is wrong, the bare excepts hide it and tests fail elsewhere with no stack pointing here.

[ADVISORY] The discover-dataset eligibility heuristic requires a literal 'event.type:error' substring in the raw query string, so the many discover queries that return error events without that token (empty query, error.* field filters, error_type filters) are silently excluded from upsampling. On an allowlisted sampled project, two widgets over the same time range show different totals — one with the sampled count multiplied by ~10, one with the raw undercount — and the docstring's 'err on the side of caution' note documents the mechanism but not this user-visible inconsistency; the author's strongest rebuttal is that this is a deliberate conservative default, which holds only if the inconsistent-numbers outcome was explicitly accepted, which nothing in the diff shows.

[BUG] _is_error_focused_query gates the sample_weight transform on a raw substring match of 'event.type:error' in the query string, so any query containing that literal as a negation, quoted literal, or OR-branch (e.g. '!event.type:error', 'message:"event.type:error"', 'event.type:transaction OR event.type:error') is treated as error-focused while its result set includes non-error rows. On an allowlisted org, a user issuing such a discover-dataset query gets upsampled_count() = sum(sample_weight) computed over transaction rows where sample_weight is null/absent, silently returning zero or partially-weighted counts instead of real counts (or a Snuba aggregate error surfaced as a 500); the normalization-mismatch defeats the 'errors only' control exactly the way the lens describes.

[BUG] The 'upsampled_count' SnQLFunction is registered only in discover.py's function_converter, but _should_apply_sample_weight_transform (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:112-113) applies the column transform unconditionally for the errors dataset, whose query builder has no such function registered. Any events-stats request with dataset=errors against an allowlisted org gets yAxis 'upsampled_count() as count' sent to a query builder that cannot parse that function, failing query construction and returning a 500 for every such request rather than stats data.

[ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no call site anywhere in this diff, so the documented invalidation contract ('should be called when the allowlist configuration changes') is unfulfilled and the helper is dead code. After an admin edits the project_allowlist option, eligibility answers stay stale for up to 60 seconds per (org, project-set) key; and because the cache key is derived from the full sorted project-id tuple, an invalidator that passes only the changed project's ids can never match existing cached combos, so partial invalidation is structurally impossible even once a caller is wired up — operators flipping the allowlist get silently wrong counts in the interim.

[ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies the client-supplied contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate into sample_rate with no bounds check (any truthy float is accepted, only parse failures are swallowed), establishing that the value feeding the sample_weight/upsampled_count pipeline is unvalidated client input. A SDK holder (or any actor with a project DSN) can report an arbitrarily small or large sample rate, and the new upsampled_count() = sum(sample_weight) aggregation amplifies that untrusted value into organization-visible counts — dashboards and alerts on allowlisted projects can be inflated or zeroed at will by the event sender.

[BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the exact bare string 'count()' (after lower/strip), so an aliased form like 'count() as foo' — a valid yAxis in this API — is passed through untransformed while an unaliased count() in the same request is rewritten to upsampled_count(). A single request mixing 'count()' and 'count() as foo' on an allowlisted org returns one column weighted by sample_weight and the other as raw count, silently producing two different 'count' numbers in the same response; callers relying on aliased counts get undercounts with no error.

[ADVISORY] The public entrypoint is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects — including the 60s cache read/write path, the hash-based cache key construction, and the cached-hit short-circuit that re-evaluates _should_apply_sample_weight_transform — has no test in this diff; the new tests bypass it and call the private helpers directly. adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`'s docstring claims the allowlist is read fresh each time and that results can change between calls during request processing to ensure the “latest configuration state.” However, its only visible caller in this diff, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, caches the eligibility result for 60 seconds (`cache.get/set` on `error_upsampling_eligible:...`), meaning the effective behavior for typical usage is *not* “latest configuration state” and will not change between calls within that TTL. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The upsampling decision is made by string-munging query columns inside one endpoint instead of at the dataset/search-resolver layer where dataset and project context already live, leaving every other error-count surface for the same org on the raw sampled path. For an allowlisted org, the events-stats chart shows upsampled counts while dashboards built on the organization_events endpoint, issue/search counts, and alert queries over the same time window show raw sampled counts — mutually inconsistent numbers for the same data. Anchoring the transform at the resolver layer (where the discover/errors dataset split and per-project context are already available) would make it apply uniformly and eliminate the endpoint-side dataset-sniffing and substring query parsing altogether.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds error-upsampling behavior by transforming `count()` to `upsampled_count()` only within `OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint._get_event_stats` (via `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` in `src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py`). No other endpoints or shared resolver/dataset query-building paths are updated to apply the same transform, even though the new SnQL function is added at the Discover dataset layer (`src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`). This makes the reviewer’s architectural concern diff-grounded: the upsampling decision is endpoint-specific rather than centralized, which can lead to inconsistent counts across other query surfaces that still use raw `count()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query uses raw substring matching, so negated or compound discover queries such as '!event.type:error' or '(event.type:error OR event.type:transaction)' are classified as error-focused and get count() replaced with sum(sample_weight) over rows that have no sample_weight. For allowlisted projects, a query excluding errors (e.g. !event.type:error on discover) has its transaction counts silently transformed to sum over a missing/zero sample_weight column, returning 0 or a query error instead of the raw counts the non-allowlisted path returns for the identical query.

Since `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` uses `_is_error_focused_query` for the `discover` dataset, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` can enable upsampling and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` will rewrite `count()` to `upsampled_count()` (summing `sample_weight`) even when the discover query is effectively excluding errors / returning non-error rows. Given the module comment that `sample_weight` doesn't exist for transactions, this can produce wrong results or query errors for such queries.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`, the new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is added without `private=True` (unlike nearby internal functions which explicitly set `private=True`). Because the function is registered on the Discover dataset and not marked private, the diff supports the finding that users could invoke `upsampled_count()` in arbitrary Discover queries (including non-error contexts), potentially causing query failures or incorrect results when `sample_weight` isn't present.

Therefore, discover queries that still yield error events but don’t include that exact token (e.g., other field filters or empty query) will not be upsampled, creating a potentially surprising inconsistency across otherwise similar widgets. This is an edge-case/UX-consistency concern grounded in the code, even if the docstring frames it as conservative behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query gates the sample_weight transform on a raw substring match of 'event.type:error' in the query string, so any query containing that literal as a negation, quoted literal, or OR-branch (e.g. '!event.type:error', 'message:"event.type:error"', 'event.type:transaction OR event.type:error') is treated as error-focused while its result set includes non-error rows. On an allowlisted org, a user issuing such a discover-dataset query gets upsampled_count() = sum(sample_weight) computed over transaction rows where sample_weight is null/absent, silently returning zero or partially-weighted counts instead of real counts (or a Snuba aggregate error surfaced as a 500); the normalization-mismatch defeats the 'errors only' control exactly the way the lens describes.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_is_error_focused_query` returns True purely via `if "event.type:error" in query:` on the raw query string. That value is used in `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` for the `discover` dataset, which then enables `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` to rewrite `count()` into `upsampled_count() as count`. The added `upsampled_count` aggregate in `discover.py` is `sum(sample_weight)` and the helper’s own comment states sample_weight “doesn't exist for transactions.” Because the check is a substring match, queries like `!event.type:error`, a quoted literal containing `event.type:error`, or mixed queries (e.g. `event.type:transaction OR event.type:error`) will incorrectly be treated as error-focused, causing `sum(sample_weight)` to be applied to non-error rows and yielding wrong counts or potential query errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache has no call site anywhere in this diff, so the documented invalidation contract ('should be called when the allowlist configuration changes') is unfulfilled and the helper is dead code. After an admin edits the project_allowlist option, eligibility answers stay stale for up to 60 seconds per (org, project-set) key; and because the cache key is derived from the full sorted project-id tuple, an invalidator that passes only the changed project's ids can never match existing cached combos, so partial invalidation is structurally impossible even once a caller is wired up — operators flipping the allowlist get silently wrong counts in the interim.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, but there is no call site shown anywhere in the PR, so it is currently unused/dead code. The helper also caches allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds (`cache.set(..., 60)` in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`), so without wiring invalidation into whatever updates `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, changes can remain stale until TTL expiry. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies the client-supplied contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate into sample_rate with no bounds check (any truthy float is accepted, only parse failures are swallowed), establishing that the value feeding the sample_weight/upsampled_count pipeline is unvalidated client input. A SDK holder (or any actor with a project DSN) can report an arbitrarily small or large sample rate, and the new upsampled_count() = sum(sample_weight) aggregation amplifies that untrusted value into organization-visible counts — dashboards and alerts on allowlisted projects can be inflated or zeroed at will by the event sender.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` in `src/sentry/testutils/factories.py`, which unconditionally sets `normalized_data["sample_rate"] = float(client_sample_rate)` from client-controlled `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` with no bounds/range validation (only parse errors are swallowed; any nonzero/truthy value is accepted). Separately, the diff introduces `upsampled_count()` in `discover.py` as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, and `organization_events_stats.py` rewrites `count()` queries to `upsampled_count()` for allowlisted error queries. The new tests assert that sending `client_sample_rate: 0.1` yields counts of 10, demonstrating that the client-provided sample rate affects the effective weight/count pipeline. Given this, the lack of validation on client-supplied sample rate is a real integrity/security defect: a sender with a DSN can manipulate organization-visible counts by choosing extreme sample_rate values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the exact bare string 'count()' (after lower/strip), so an aliased form like 'count() as foo' — a valid yAxis in this API — is passed through untransformed while an unaliased count() in the same request is rewritten to upsampled_count(). A regression in the cache-hit early return (wrong cache key, `cached_result and ...` short-circuit inverting a False cache, stale 60s decisions) ships unverified, and the 60-second staleness behavior is untested.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds new public helper `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` with caching logic (`cached_result = cache.get(...)` and early return on cache hit). The new unit test file `tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py` only exercises private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`) and never calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. The endpoint tests in `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py` do trigger the wrapper indirectly via `organization_events_stats.py`, but they do not pre-populate the cache, so the cache-hit branch (`if cached_result is not None: ...`) is not executed by any test shown. This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap for the new caching/early-return behavior, not a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every new API test patches sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options, so the suite verifies the mock, not the real configuration surface: nothing in the diff registers the option key 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' in sentry's option registry, and no test checks options.get resolves it. If the option key is not registered (no registration appears anywhere in this diff), production options.get returns the default [] forever, upsampling never activates, and the feature is inert — while all tests pass green because they inject the allowlist through the mock.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper reads `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` in `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, but the added tests consistently patch `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options` (e.g. in `tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py` and `tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py`) to force allowlist behavior. Within this diff, there is no visible option registration for the key, and no test exercises the real `options.get`/option-registry surface (i.e., behavior without the mock). While the claim that the option is *not* registered elsewhere cannot be verified from this diff alone, the finding correctly identifies that the new tests would pass even if the option key were misconfigured or unregistered in production.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache ships with no caller anywhere in the diff and no test, so its key-construction correctness is unverified and the invalidation path is dead code. When the allowlist changes, no code path calls this function (allowlisted projects see stale upsampled/unupsampled decisions for up to 60s), and if a caller is added later, any drift between this key format and the one in is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects (e.g. the hash(tuple(sorted(...))) construction duplicated in two places) would make invalidation a silent no-op with no test to catch it.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is newly added in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` but there is no reference/call site added anywhere else in the shown changes, and the new tests (`tests/sentry/api/helpers/test_error_upsampling.py` and the endpoint tests) do not exercise this invalidation function or verify its cache-key format. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites the exact string 'count()' (case/space-stripped); aliased forms like 'count() as total' pass through untransformed, and no test in the diff covers any non-bare count() yAxis variant. A dashboard or API caller passing 'count() as count_total' on an allowlisted project gets a regular unweighted count in the same response where bare count() is upsampled — inconsistent numbers presented as one series; test_transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only tests bare 'count()', 'COUNT()', and ' count() ', so the passthrough branch for aliased or decorated columns is both unimplemented and unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, the rewrite triggers only when `column.lower().strip() == "count()"`, so strings like `"count() as total"` or other decorated/aliased count expressions will not be transformed and will remain an unweighted `count()` even when `upsampling_enabled` is true (used in `organization_events_stats.py` via `final_columns`). The added tests only cover bare `count()` variants (`"count()"`, `"COUNT()"`, and whitespace), and do not cover aliased/decorated cases, so this inconsistent behavior (upsampled vs non-upsampled depending on yAxis formatting) is both present and unverified in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The gating returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset (`if dataset == errors: return True`), but the `upsampled_count` SnQL function is only registered in discover.py's function_converter, so errors-dataset queries emit a function the errors dataset schema does not define. Once the allowlist option is set, any organization_events_stats request with dataset=errors (or any errors-dataset query path reaching this transform) sends `upsampled_count() as count` to Snuba's errors dataset, which has no such function registered; the query is rejected as an unknown function and the stats endpoint returns an error instead of counts for allowlisted projects.

adjudication.rationale: In `error_upsampling.py`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns `True` unconditionally for `dataset == errors`. When `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` returns true, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `"upsampled_count() as count"` and `organization_events_stats.py` then passes those columns into the timeseries/top-events queries. However, this diff only registers the `upsampled_count` SnQL function in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`'s `function_converter`; there is no corresponding registration shown for the errors dataset. Based on the diff alone, an errors-dataset query can therefore be transformed to use `upsampled_count()` without that function being defined for that dataset, which would cause query rejection/endpoint failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The transform assumes `sample_weight` exists for all events in allowlisted projects ('no additional null checks are needed'), but the diff contains no backfill for pre-existing events, and ClickHouse sum() silently skips NULL/missing sample_weight values. The moment the allowlist option is enabled, every historical event in an allowlisted project (ingested before the sample_weight-producing consumer was deployed) contributes nothing to sum(sample_weight): dashboard time buckets covering the pre-backfill window silently report 0 or partial counts instead of the true error count, with no error surfaced to users — a silent miscount of production data with no migration or backfill step anywhere in the diff to prevent it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `upsampled_count()` implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` and explicitly states it “assumes sample_weight exists for all events in allowlisted projects” with “no additional null checks” (new `SnQLFunction` in `discover.py` and comments in `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`). The diff itself does not include any migration/backfill or defensive fallback (e.g., `coalesce(sample_weight, 1)` or conditional use based on data freshness) to ensure historical rows have non-null `sample_weight`. While the claimed production impact depends on the existing ClickHouse schema/defaults and historical ingestion behavior (not shown in the diff), the review concern is concretely grounded in the new assumption and lack of safeguards in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `upsampled_count` aggregate reads `Column("sample_weight")`, but this changeset contains no schema-change artifact (migration, Snuba schema update, or expand step) that adds `sample_weight` to any storage schema, and no dual-write/expand-then-contract phase gating the read on the column actually existing everywhere. This is a rolling-deploy skew: if the option is enabled (or the code ships with the option later flipped) before the Snuba events schema carries `sample_weight`, every count() query for allowlisted projects fails with an unknown-identifier error; there is no migration in this diff to sequence against and no guard in `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` to fall back to plain count() when the column is absent, so the failure mode is all-or-nothing per deployment window.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new SnQL aggregate `upsampled_count` that unconditionally compiles to `sum(Column("sample_weight"))` in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`, and the endpoint wiring can replace `count()` with `upsampled_count()` via `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` with no fallback if `sample_weight` is unavailable. However, the finding’s core claim—that `sample_weight` is not yet present in Snuba storage and that this PR must include a schema/migration/expand step—cannot be verified from the diff alone (the column may already exist outside this changeset). What is verifiable is the lack of any defensive guard/feature gating against schema skew while introducing a hard dependency on `sample_weight`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `invalidate_upsampling_cache` has no caller anywhere in this diff and its cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`, so an allowlist change cannot actually be invalidated (the caller would need to reconstruct the exact key for every org/project combination that ever queried). The function ships as a documented consistency mechanism ('should be called when the allowlist configuration changes') that nothing calls and that could not deliver consistency even if called; operators who rely on the docstring will expect allowlist changes to take effect immediately, but stale eligibility persists up to 60 seconds (or indefinitely if the cached key's project set no longer matches), and the next maintainer extending the cache semantics inherits a dead parallel path to keep in sync.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is introduced in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py` but is not called anywhere else in the shown changes, while its docstring claims it “should be called when the allowlist configuration changes.” Also, the cache key is derived from the *queried* `project_ids` set (`hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`), so a config-change hook would have to know and delete every cached subset key that may exist, which is not realistically achievable from the information shown. However, the finding’s “indefinitely” staleness claim is not supported by the diff because the cache is always written with a 60s TTL (`cache.set(..., 60)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _is_error_focused_query matches 'event.type:error' as a raw substring of the query string, so negated or compound queries like '!event.type:error' or 'event.type:transaction OR event.type:error' are classified as error-focused. A discover-dataset request with '!event.type:error' (transactions only) from an allowlisted org gets count() rewritten to upsampled_count() as count, so the query aggregates sum(sample_weight) over transaction rows where sample_weight does not exist — the endpoint either returns a Snuba error (500 on a previously valid request) or silently reports zero/incorrect counts with a 200.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_is_error_focused_query` returns True based solely on the raw substring check `if "event.type:error" in query` after lowercasing. This will incorrectly classify queries like `!event.type:error` or compound queries containing that substring as “error-focused”. For the `discover` dataset, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` uses `_is_error_focused_query`, so this misclassification can enable `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`, which rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count`. The new `upsampled_count` in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py` computes `sum(sample_weight)`, while the code comments explicitly state `sample_weight` doesn't exist for transactions; thus a discover query that excludes errors (e.g. `!event.type:error`) can be rewritten to reference a non-existent column for the remaining (transaction) rows, causing Snuba errors or incorrect results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True for the errors dataset unconditionally, but the upsampled_count SnQL function is only registered in the discover dataset's function_converter (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py), leaving the errors dataset path with an unresolvable function. When dataset=errors is requested for an allowlisted org, the transform emits 'upsampled_count() as count' which the errors dataset query path cannot resolve, turning a previously working stats request into a 500 as soon as the project is added to the allowlist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` return `True` whenever `dataset == errors` (in `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`), and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` rewrites `count()` into `"upsampled_count() as count"`. In this PR, the only added SnQL function registration for `upsampled_count` is in the Discover dataset (`src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`). The diff does not show any corresponding registration for the Errors dataset, so an Errors-dataset query that gets transformed to `upsampled_count()` would plausibly fail to resolve the function and error at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] upsampled_count computes toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) assuming sample_weight is populated for every event in allowlisted projects, but events ingested before the column existed or without the error_sampling context have no sample_weight, so sum() over nulls yields 0. For an allowlisted project with historical events lacking sample_weight, the stats endpoint returns 200 with count 0 for buckets that actually contain events — silently wrong chart data presented as success, and the code comment itself admits this assumption rather than guarding it (e.g. coalesce(sample_weight, 1)).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `count()` to `upsampled_count()` for allowlisted error queries (`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`), and defines `upsampled_count` as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` in `discover.py` without any null/default handling. The code comments explicitly assume `sample_weight` always exists/is populated for all events in allowlisted projects, but the diff itself does not prove that invariant (no coalesce/defaulting, no migration/schema enforcement shown). This is a concrete, diff-grounded correctness risk/edge case, but the claim about historical events definitely producing silent 0 counts cannot be verified solely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code — no caller exists anywhere in this diff, so the documented cache-consistency contract is unfulfilled. When an operator adds or removes a project from the allowlist, the 60-second cached eligibility is never proactively invalidated; operators who rely on the docstring's promise ('should be called when the allowlist configuration changes') find no hook to call, and the stale upsampled-vs-raw count behavior persists for up to a minute with no signal.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)` is newly added but is not referenced anywhere in the provided diff (no call sites shown). Meanwhile `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...)` caches allowlist eligibility for 60s (`cache.set(..., 60)`), and the invalidation function’s docstring claims it “should be called when the allowlist configuration changes”. With no hook/caller in this diff, that documented proactive invalidation path is effectively unimplemented (though the TTL still bounds staleness to 60s), making this a real diff-grounded maintenance/contract issue rather than a guaranteed functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _are_all_projects_error_upsampled does `project_id in allowlist` with no type normalization or logging, so an allowlist configured as strings (how JSON options are typically authored) never matches integer project IDs. Upsampling silently no-ops for the entire deployment — every query falls back to raw count() while operators believe the feature is enabled — and because the negative result is cached for 60 seconds and nothing is logged, the misconfiguration is invisible; debugging requires noticing that downsampled counts look suspiciously low.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` does `project_id in allowlist` where `project_id` is an `int` (from `snuba_params.project_ids`) and `allowlist` is whatever `options.get(...)` returns. The diff shows no normalization (e.g., casting allowlist entries to `int`) and no logging/metrics when eligibility is false. If the option is configured with string IDs, membership checks will fail and upsampling will never enable, with the negative result cached for 60s in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`, making diagnosis harder. Whether options are “typically” strings isn’t proven by the diff, but the lack of normalization/observability is a concrete robustness/operability gap introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The identical `if upsampling_enabled: final_columns = transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(query_columns)` block is hand-repeated at three sites (top-events branch, RPC non-top branch, standard non-top branch) even though the transformation is idempotent and could be applied once right after should_upsample is computed. The next change to the transformation (e.g. handling count_if or a new alias rule) must be replicated in three places inside one function; missing one produces silently divergent columns between the top-events and plain-timeseries paths for the same request — exactly the drift this parallel-branch shape invites.

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats.py` inside `_get_event_stats`, the diff repeats the same conditional transformation in three separate branches: (1) inside the `top_events > 0` path before `run_top_events_timeseries_query` / `top_events_timeseries`, (2) inside the `use_rpc` non-top-events path before `run_timeseries_query`, and (3) in the standard non-RPC non-top-events path before `timeseries_query`. The transform function shown (`transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`) is effectively idempotent for the introduced rewrite (only rewrites exact `count()`), so applying it once after `should_upsample` is computed would avoid branch divergence and reduce maintenance risk. This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability concern rather than a verified correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling checks `if client_sample_rate:` (truthiness instead of presence), so a client_sample_rate of 0.0 — a value in the field's numeric domain — is silently treated as absent, and both failure paths are bare `except Exception: pass`. A test fixture storing client_sample_rate 0.0 gets no sample_rate field and no signal why, so a test exercising the zero-rate boundary silently tests the wrong thing; the swallowed exceptions also mean a malformed contexts structure (e.g. contexts=None raising AttributeError) is indistinguishable from 'rate not present'.
